text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the lung arteries, which forces the right side of the heart to work harder and leads to reduced oxygen and blood flow.
snippet_highlighted_words: high blood pressure in the lung arteries

list.snippet: Shortness of breath (dyspnea): Often starts during physical activity like climbing stairs or exercising, and can eventually happen even at rest.
Fatigue and weakness: Feeling unusually tired or drained during normal daily tasks.
Chest pain or pressure: Caused by the extra strain on the heart muscle.
Dizziness or lightheadedness: Especially when standing up or exerting yourself.
Fainting (syncope): Occurs as heart strain and blood flow limitations become more severe.
Heart palpitations: A fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat.
Swelling (edema): Fluid buildup in the ankles, feet, legs, or abdomen due to heart strain.
Cyanosis: A bluish or grayish tint to the lips, fingers, or skin from low oxygen levels.

text_blocks.snippet: PAH symptoms are often mild or nonexistent in the early stages and mimic other heart or lung conditions. As the disease progresses, daily activities become much harder.
You should seek emergency medical care if you experience:

list.snippet: A fast heart rate that will not slow down
Shortness of breath that does not go away with rest
